messages:
sam: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak I see ~12% CPU increase on host ingress and p90 up ~40ms. Repro on load test. Anyone else?
perfbot: perf-run 2026-03-18T03:12Z: host-ingest path +11% CPU, p90 +40ms (run id: perf-175678)
nana: can you drop the perf link + diff? Did the change touch batching heuristics too? @ben?
sam: perf artifacts: https://perf.redwood/internal/175678, main diff: KernelSelector now prefers fused-attn for seq <= 64 (was <=32). suspect extra probe/fallbacks for mid-lengths.
ben: ran perf top while reproing. hot functions:
    23.1% grpc::Writev
    18.7% HostParser::tokenize
    12.4% KernelSelector::probe_cpu
    9.2% std::mutex::lock
looks like more syscall/writev pressure + tokenization still expensive.
lisa: KV cache metrics spiked same timeframe — evict/sec jumped 1.2k -> 4.5k. Shard hotness looks correlated by origin. Maybe sequence-change increased KV miss churn.
mike: quick local A/B: revert selector threshold to old (<=32) -> p95 drops 28ms. So selector change is a big suspect. Want to canary rollback?
nana: before full rollback, try two mitigations: 1) reduce batching window for small sequences (batch_max_wait_ms: 3) to cut wait amplification, 2) bump kv cache shard count to reduce eviction hotspots. Also add coalescing for grpc writev on host proxy.
ben: have a patch that enables writev coalesce + batch_max_wait_ms: 3 for short sequences. Local microbench: CPU -6%, p90 -18ms. Patch: git://repo/host/patches/ingest-coalesce-175678. Config snippet:
```
route:
  small_seq:
    match: seq_len <= 64
    batch_max_wait_ms: 3
    writev_coalesce: true
```

sam: :thumbsup: plan: canary ben's patch in zone-a, monitor kv_evict/sec, grpc write latency, and tokenization CPU. Also run eval prompt-set to ensure output quality unchanged (kernel diff might change generation order). @ana please add rollout plan.
nana: will add tests and a ramp plan. adding alert for writev_queue_length and kv_eviction_rate. also enable 30s flamegraph sampling during canary.
perfbot: canary deployed to zone-a at 1756789180 by ci/cd. collecting 10k requests for telemetry.
lisa: noted, will watch kv shards and evict counters.
mike: if canary looks good, we can either keep coalesce + smaller window or revert selector and re-evaluate fused-attn threshold with more checks.
sam: agree. if canary fails, immediate rollback path = restore selector threshold + remove coalesce. keeping both mitigations separate in case of signal inversion.
